pages.title: The atelier
pages.content:
Aurum & Pearl is a small atelier with one long bench, two windows and a jeweller who still files every claw by hand. We began by remaking family pieces for friends, and found that what people wanted most was not more sparkle, but jewellery that felt personal and lasted.

Our gold is recycled and refined in Europe, our diamonds are lab-grown and certified, and our pearls are chosen one at a time from a family farm we have worked with for years. Every piece is finished, polished and checked at our own bench before it is wrapped.

We make things to be worn every day, and handed down one day.

The atelier

Appointments in the atelier are available on Thursdays and Saturdays, for engagement rings, engraving and remodelling old pieces.

posts.title: Caring for pearls
posts.excerpt: Last on, first off: the simple habits that keep a pearl glowing for a lifetime.
posts.content:
Pearls are organic gems, made in layers by a living creature, and they are softer than any stone. That is what gives them their glow, and it is also why they need a little more care than gold or diamonds.

Put your pearls on last, after perfume, hairspray and creams, and take them off first. After wearing, wipe them with a soft, slightly damp cloth and let them dry flat before putting them away, never in an airtight bag, because pearls like a little moisture in the air.

Store them apart from other jewellery so harder pieces cannot scratch them, and wear them often: the natural oils of your skin are the best polish there is. Once a year, bring them to the atelier and we will check the clasp and settings for free.

posts.title: Choosing a solitaire
posts.excerpt: Cut first, then colour, then carat: how we help people choose a ring they will love for decades.
posts.content:
When people come to the atelier for an engagement ring, they usually start by asking about size. We gently suggest starting with the cut instead: a well-cut stone of half a carat will look brighter and livelier than a larger stone cut poorly.

Next comes colour. In yellow gold, a stone with the faintest warmth disappears into the setting beautifully, so there is no need to pay for the very whitest grades. In platinum or white gold, a whiter stone makes more sense.

Finally, think about how the ring will be worn. A higher setting catches more light; a lower one is kinder to gloves and jumpers. We always make a wax model first, so you can try the shape on your hand before a single gram of gold is cast.

posts.title: A day at the bench
posts.excerpt: Forty-two settings, a loupe and a lot of tea: how a tennis bracelet is made.
posts.content:
A tennis bracelet looks simple: a line of stones that moves like water. Making one takes about four days at the bench, most of them spent on the tiny claws that hold each diamond.

First the links are cast and joined, so the bracelet can bend without gaps. Then each of the forty-two settings is cut by hand under a loupe, a stone is placed, and four claws are pushed over and rounded so they will never catch on a sleeve.

The last day is for polishing, testing the clasp a few hundred times and a final check of every claw. Then it is cleaned, photographed for our records and wrapped, ready to be worn for the next fifty years.

products.name: Solitaire Ring
products.description:
A single round brilliant lab-grown diamond of 0.5 carat, held high in a slender six-claw setting on a band of 18 ct recycled yellow gold. The gallery is pierced with a tiny arch so light reaches the stone from below.

Each ring is made to order in our workshop in about three weeks and arrives with a grading certificate. Complimentary resizing within the first year.
products.short_description: A half-carat lab-grown diamond in a six-claw setting of 18 ct recycled gold.

reviews.author: Eleanor
reviews.content: He proposed with it on a cold beach and I have not stopped looking at it since. The setting is so delicate.

reviews.author: Priya
reviews.content: Exquisite, and the team helped us choose the right size over the phone. It arrived in a beautiful box.
